newsitem.title: albania: German evacuees in Albania cross-fire.
newsitem.headline: German evacuees in Albania cross-fire.

text.p: German troops exchange fire with Albanian gunmen during a perilous rescue of Western residents from an airfield near Tirana on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen started shooting at evacuees and German military helicopters, and the German soldiers fire back, a diplomatic source said. An Albanian was lightly wounded but no foreigners were hurt.

Officials in Bonn and diplomats in Tirana said five military helicopters sent in from Bosnia evacuated 120 people, mostly Germans and citizens of other European Union states, to Montenegro on Albania's northern border.
German military spokesmen in Bonn said there was a bullet hole in one of the German helicopters.
The mass evacuation of foreigners from the Albanian capital has proved to be a dangerous undertaking.
The United States suspended its operation after one of its helicopters came under fire from a surface-to-air missile and an Italian helicopter also came under fire.

Pictures from a Turkish television crew obtained by Reuters television showed German troops from the SFOR forces in Bosnia first hitting the ground when gunmen opened fire from a van and then shooting back as evacuees boarded the helicopters.
The television footage showed several of the evacuees cowering on the tarmac at an airfield near the capital. Some were praying.

"It was a very difficult operation," German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe told journalists in Bonn. "We originally planned to land in front of the American embassy. But the Americans broke off the evacuation when their helicopters were fired on when they were on the way."
The diplomatic source said the evacuees were taken to the Montenegran capital of Podgorica. They were due to be flown to Cologne in Germany later on Friday.
Diplomatic sources said they had opted for evacuation by helicopter as it was proving too dangerous on Albanian roads among large numbers of uncontrolled gunmen. Five Germans decided to stay behind.

"There is apparently anarchy in all parts of the country," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in Bonn. "There is no apparent control anymore by the security forces, ministries or the administration. The security situation is completely confused and changes by the hour."

In Washington, a defence official announced that the United States had suspended its military evacuation of Americans after a Marine Cobra helicopter reported being fired on by a missile from the ground.
Another Cobra came under small-arms fire and returned the fire, the official said. Neither U.S. aircraft was hit. Officials said 480 U.S. nationals had been evacuated before the suspension.
